raw_text:
Review of run r-20260922T095849575314-serve-provenance (plan imas-ambix:serve-telemetry-spine,
section 3, serve-config landing note), read at its head 0665bb9937e9c15c8f250fe4ca3615a72524eb79
against base 782cc5f20c441ef57c58634142ab85739201cc6e. Nothing here re-runs the worker's
implementation; the gate, the mutation and the four stated questions were checked against the
landed artifacts and, where the artifact is a live capture, against the live engine.

The change adds a fifth sparse section, serve_config, to the receipt row: ROW_SCHEMA_VERSION
moves 2 to 3 (imas_ambix/agent/serving_receipts.py:98), serve_config joins ROW_SECTIONS (:103),
a fixed seven-key vocabulary SERVE_CONFIG_OPTIONS is declared once (:112), read_serve_config
(:374) asks the engine's GET /server_info, _merge_serve_config (:408) lets the engine win over a
caller's --serve-setting, and record_receipts (:566-576) resolves it once per serve and carries
it on every row (:587).

FIRST QUESTION — the artifact records hostname 98dci4-srv-1006.iter.org (the login node) while
the done-when asked for a row recorded against the live engine on the GPU node. The artifact
does demonstrate that claim, and recording it from the login node changes no engine-derived
value in it. The row's hostname names the recording host by construction, not the engine's host
(hostname=hostname or local_hostname() at serving_receipts.py:339; record_receipts sets it from
local_hostname() when no probe is attached, :558), and 98dci4-srv-1006.iter.org is this login
node's own name (`hostname -f`). The seven settings and the engine section came over HTTP from
the live engine: job 1273253 is RUNNING on 98dci4-gpu-0003 (`squeue -j 1273253`), and a review-time
GET of http://98dci4-gpu-0003:18810/server_info returns all seven at top level with exactly the
values on the row — context_length 512000, max_total_tokens 4000000, mem_fraction_static 0.85,
max_running_requests 36, hicache_ratio 2.0, speculative_algorithm "DSPARK", tp_size 4. What the
login-node vantage does change is confined to the recorder side, and the manifest and the landed
record both state it: the host section is absent because --no-node-probe was passed, and the
container identity (job_id 1273253, profile_slug/served_name deepseek-v4-1-flash, gpus 4) was
supplied as launcher arguments read from the job record rather than from a sidecar's own
environment. One limit of the artifact should be read with it: it is not a row the deployed
sidecar wrote. The recorder running in job 1273253 is still the pre-change code — its own file
/work/projects/imas_gpu/agents/receipts/deepseek-v4-1-flash-1273253.jsonl holds 79,116 rows with
no schema_version and no sections, last written 2026-09-22T10:28:24Z — so the capture shows the
new code against the live engine, not the new code on the node. The done-when's words ("a row
recorded against the live engine on the GPU node") are satisfied by what the artifact is, and the
artifact states its vantage rather than letting a reader assume otherwise.

SECOND QUESTION — every prefix_cache and spec field on that row is null while the fields carry
numbers in some rows the recorder writes. This is a scrape gap tied to the engine build, not a
login-node artefact and not an absence of the phenomenon. The evidence, all produced at review
time: (a) the recorder's own parser, run against the live exposition fetched from the engine,
returns counters {generation_tokens, prompt_tokens} and no prefix-cache key at all, with
spec_decode draft_tokens_total / accepted_tokens_total / num_accepted_per_pos all None; (b) the
live exposition publishes no prefix_cache family whatsoever (0 occurrences of "prefix_cache" in
1,236 lines) and its speculative families are spec_accept_rate and spec_accept_length gauges,
not the draft/accepted token counters the row asks for; (c) the on-node recorder's own rows for
the same job carry the same six prefix_cache and four spec fields null at both the first row
(2026-09-17T20:00:00Z) and the last (2026-09-22T10:28:24Z), so the identical nulls are written
from the GPU node; and (d) across the receipts directory the discriminator is the profile, not
the host — every deepseek-v4-1-flash job file (15 of them) is null in those fields while every
deepseek-v4-flash job file (7 of them) carries numbers. The fields are therefore a recorder
vocabulary that this engine build does not publish; a null here means the metric family is
absent from the exposition, not that caching or speculative decoding is off, and the build does
report cache_hit_rate (0.0) and cached_tokens_total by cache_source in
sglang:cache_hit_rate / sglang:cached_tokens_total. The pre-change rows carry the same nulls, so
this is not this node's defect; the row's own engine section parsed fully (histograms, cached
prompt tokens by tier), so the scrape itself reached and understood the endpoint.

THIRD QUESTION — all seven settings are present in the row under serve_config. Six resolve from
the launch-flag vocabulary by the ordinary dash-to-underscore transform: --context-length,
--max-total-tokens, --mem-fraction-static, --max-running-requests, --hicache-ratio and
--speculative-algorithm. The seventh is the engine's own spelling: tp_size, which corresponds to
--tensor-parallel-size and shares no lexical root with it. A reader who knows only the launch
flags cannot resolve tp_size from the row; the nearest bridge in the landed change is the plan's
prose "tensor-parallel width" (docs/plans/serve-telemetry-spine.html:366) a few lines above the
vocabulary list, which implies the correspondence without stating it, and neither the evidence
record's table (which has a Setting/Value/Source column, no flag name) nor the module comment
states it either. Hence the finding below.

FOURTH QUESTION — all seven came from the engine, and none had to come from elsewhere, so no
--serve-setting was passed for the capture. Verified rather than accepted: the live /server_info
carries all seven at top level of its 502-key object, and the row's values match it exactly
(values quoted above); read_serve_config keeps only keys present and non-None (:400-405), and the
resolution is made once (test_record_receipts_reads_the_serve_config_from_the_engine_once,
tests/test_agent_serving_receipts.py:1364, asserts exactly one /server_info call across two
ticks). On the omission rule: a setting the engine does not report is left out rather than written
as null — _merge_serve_config returns None when neither source read anything (:424), build_receipt_row
turns an empty mapping into an absent section (:367), and two tests cover it
(test_read_serve_config_omits_a_setting_the_engine_left_out,
test_receipt_row_omits_an_unread_serve_configuration). In this particular row none of the seven is
omitted, so the omission branch is not exercised by the live artifact itself — it is exercised by
the tests, and I read the two tests rather than assuming them. The negative control covers the
precedence claim only (engine over caller), not the omission claim; the omission claim's evidence
is the pair of tests plus the code path, which I read.
